IQ-CAL-001.name_en: Caliph al-Mansur/Baghdad Caliphs: Islamic Legal Caliphate Governance & Imperial Order
IQ-CAL-001.description_en: Abu Ja'far Abdullah al-Mansur (714-775), 2nd Abbasid Caliph, built Round City of Baghdad (762), established proto-separation of powers 'Caliph-Vizier-Diwan': Caliph holds supreme religious/military authority, Vizier (chief minister) heads administration, Diwan (departments) divide jurisdiction. Core governance tech: Islamic law (Fiqh) legislative/judicial unification, Bayt al-Mal (treasury) fiscal centralization, four Sunni madhhabs (Maliki/Hanafi/Shafi'i/Hanbali) coexist & compete, Bay'ah (oath of allegiance) as political legitimacy. Exemplifies M160 Islamic Legal/Caliphal Governance—divine law as constitution, scholar class as bureaucracy, oath of allegiance as political contract.
IQ-CAL-001.reason_en: Abbasid Caliphate not theocratic autocracy but trinity of 'fiqh constitution + scholar bureaucracy + allegiance contract': Caliph bound by fiqh, Qadis independent adjudication, Ulama check caliphal power. M160 distinct from M149 Islamic Shura (consultative decision) and M161 Waqf Philanthropy (asset perpetuity), core: 'fiqh as constitution, scholars as bureaucracy, allegiance as contract' imperial-grade governance OS.
steps_en: Round city planning & symbolic power: 762 Round Baghdad, geometric order mirroring cosmic/fiqh order
Vizierate administrative professionalization: Islamic history's first vizier system, Diwan departmentalization (tax/military/post/judicial)
Fiqh legislation & judicial independence: Qadi appointment/removal by Caliph but judgment per fiqh non-interferable, four madhhabs compete & flourish
Treasury centralization & currency reform: Dinar/Dirham standardization, land tax (kharaj)/poll tax (jizya) systematized
Translation movement & knowledge empire: Bayt al-Hikma (House of Wisdom) translates Greek/Persian/Indian learning, Arabic becomes scientific lingua franca
IQ-CAL-001.expected_en: Early Islamic empire achieves trans-ethnic/trans-linguistic/trans-civilizational mega-scale knowledge-political integration via trinity of 'fiqh constitution + scholar bureaucracy + translation movement', governance model lasts 500 years.
IQ-CAL-001.case_en: 762 Baghdad founded -> 786-809 Harun al-Rashid golden age -> 813-833 Al-Ma'mun/Al-Mu'tasim -> 945 Buyids seize real power -> 1258 Mongols sack Baghdad, caliphate nominal but fiqh governance legacy continues today.
IQ-CAL-001.intellectual_tradition: Abbasid Fiqh Governance / Islamic Legal Theory
IQ-CAL-001.cross_cultural_impact: Madhhab system for Islamic law; Bayt al-Hikma translation model; Diwan administrative template for Ottoman/Mughal/Safavid
IQ-CAL-001.resource_curse_mitigation: Bayt al-Mal fiscal discipline; waqf endowments for public goods; agricultural tax reform

H-KZ-001-M01.description_en: Starting from personal benevolence, through the principle of 'Do not do unto others what you would not want done to yourself' (Shu), establish a universal moral practice system. Ren is the internal moral feeling, Shu is the method of extending oneself to others; together they form the core of the ethical system. Confucius' Ren-Ai is not impartial love like Mohism, but graded love starting from family ties and extending outward.
H-KZ-001-M01.source: 《论语·卫灵公》《论语·里仁》《论语·颜渊》

H-KZ-001-M02.description_en: By establishing the names and responsibilities of social roles, making names correspond to reality, build an ordered social structure. 'When names are not correct, language is not in accordance with truth; when language is not in accordance with truth, affairs cannot be carried on' is the logical starting point of political order. The logic chain: incorrect names → incoherent speech → failed affairs → rites and music falter → punishments misplaced → people at a loss. Rectification of names is not merely linguistic but normative for social roles.

H-KZ-001-M03.description_en: Grasp both extremes and apply the mean to the people. Neither excessive nor deficient, but just right. The Doctrine of the Mean is not simple compromise — compromise mechanically takes a middle value, while Zhong-Yong finds the appropriate balance point in concrete situations. 'The Doctrine of the Mean must be a virtue!' It contains two dimensions: (1) grasping both extremes to find the appropriate middle, and (2) Shi-Zhong — adjusting flexibly according to changing circumstances.

H-KZ-001-M04.description_en: Observe what a person does, consider the motive, examine where they find contentment. Teach according to individual differences in personality, ability, and interest to achieve maximum educational effectiveness. This is the earliest personalized education theory in Chinese educational history. Confucius stated 'Above average, one may be taught advanced matters; below average, one may not' and proposed heuristic teaching principles of 'do not open until the student struggles, do not clarify until the student stumbles'.

H-KZ-001-M05.description_en: 'Learning without thought is labor lost; thought without learning is perilous.' Integrate learning and thinking organically to achieve spiral cognitive ascent — this is the core of Confucian epistemology. Confucius described 'studying until forgetting food, rejoicing until forgetting sorrow, not knowing old age is coming', embodying lifelong learning-unity. It opposes both dogmatism (learning without thinking) and empiricism (thinking without learning).

H-KZ-001-M06.description_en: 'Awakened by Poetry, established by Rites, completed by Music.' Through the complete path of Poetry, Rites, and Music, achieve comprehensive personality development and cultural identity. Confucius evaluated Shao music as 'fully beautiful and fully good', while Wu music as 'fully beautiful but not fully good'. The core function is transforming external norms into moral consciousness through cultural edification.

H-KZ-001-M07.description_en: Taking the Junzi (gentleman) as ideal character, achieving moral perfection through continuous self-cultivation. 'The Junzi is open and at ease, the petty man always anxious'; 'The Junzi understands righteousness, the petty man understands profit'. The Junzi is not an identity marker but a moral ideal — anyone can reach the Junzi state through cultivation.

H-KZ-001-M08.description_en: 'No fixed course of action.' Under the premise of adhering to principles, adopt appropriate methods according to specific situations. Mencius evaluated Confucius as 'serving when he could, retiring when he should, staying long or departing swiftly' — the essence of contextual flexibility. Jing-Quan unity is key: Jing is constancy, Quan is adaptability.

H-KZ-001-M09.description_en: 'Reviewing the old to understand the new — such a person can be a teacher.' Through reviewing past knowledge, gain new understanding and achieve innovative application and transfer. Key operational points: systematically review existing knowledge, discover new meanings of old knowledge in novel contexts, achieve knowledge transfer through association and analogy. Closely related to 'infer one of three' — understanding a category of problems through one example.

H-KZ-001-M10.description_en: 'When you see a worthy person, think of equaling them; when you see an unworthy person, reflect on yourself.' Use others as mirrors for continuous self-improvement — this is the practical method for sustained growth. Transforming all people (including反面 figures) into learning resources embodies comprehensive learning wisdom. Confucius emphasized 'I examine myself three times daily', making self-reflection a daily practice.

scenarios.title: People as Sovereign: Reconstructing Ruler-Subject Relations
scenarios.description: On the foundation of traditional 'family under heaven' concept, redefine ruler-subject relations to establish the people as the political subject
scenarios.context: Facing the distortion of ruler-subject relations under autocratic rule, how to reconstruct the foundation of political legitimacy?
scenarios.challenge: How to realize the extreme expression of people-based thought within Confucian framework, maintaining traditional system while achieving power checks and balances?
scenarios.solution: 'The people as sovereign, the ruler as guest' - position the ruler as servant rather than owner, constructing political ethics centered on people's welfare
scenarios.historical_source: Waiting for Visitors under the Ming夷·On the Ruler
scenarios.modern_relevance: Provides intellectual resources for modern Chinese democratic politics, reconstructing the relationship between power and people

scenarios.title: Rule of Law First: System over Individual
scenarios.description: Critique of personal rule, establishing the priority of good laws over virtuous rulers
scenarios.context: Under the dominance of traditional virtue-based governance thought, how to establish the priority of institutional construction?
scenarios.challenge: How to argue 'good laws must precede good rulers' and break through the traditional view of 'good rulers without good laws'?
scenarios.solution: Distinguish 'laws of the world' from 'laws of one family', constrain power through good laws, preventing worst outcomes even with bad rulers
scenarios.historical_source: Waiting for Visitors under the Ming夷·On Laws
scenarios.modern_relevance: Provides historical resources for modern rule of law construction, emphasizing the priority of institutional design

scenarios.title: Lawless Law: The Art of Minimal Governance
scenarios.description: Understanding the institutional realm of 'laws become sparser yet disorder does not arise', pursuing simple and effective governance
scenarios.context: Facing an overly legalized society, how to return to the essence of institutional design?
scenarios.challenge: How to understand the profound meaning of 'three dynasties had law, post-three dynasties have no law'?
scenarios.solution: 'Hide the world within the world' - through sparse institutional design, avoid excessive intervention, achieve governance through non-action
application: Less is more in institutional design
scenarios.historical_source: Waiting for Visitors under the Ming夷·On Laws
scenarios.modern_relevance: Provides minimalist thinking for modern governance, avoiding excessive regulation

scenarios.title: Public-Private Dialectic: People's Private Interests as Public Good
scenarios.description: Re-understand public-private relations, constructing public theory based on individual interests
scenarios.context: Under traditional public-private opposition concepts, how to construct new public foundation?
scenarios.challenge: How to resolve the tension between individual interests and public interests?
scenarios.solution: 'Each may be selfish, each may benefit themselves' - aggregating all private interests creates the public good, achieving harmony between individual and collective
scenarios.historical_source: Waiting for Visitors under the Ming夷·On the Ruler
scenarios.modern_relevance: Provides theoretical foundation for modern public policy coordination of individual rights and public interests

scenarios.title: Academic Assembly: Academia Constraining Politics
scenarios.description: Design schools as political deliberation and oversight institutions
scenarios.context: How to constrain political power through academic communities?
scenarios.challenge: How to achieve political participation and supervision functions on the foundation of traditional education system?
scenarios.solution: 'Make right and wrong public in schools' - elevate schools to political decision institutions, constraining royal power through knowledge authority
scenarios.historical_source: Waiting for Visitors under the Ming夷·Schools
scenarios.modern_relevance: Provides historical reference for modern think tank construction and expert political participation

scenarios.title: Checks and Balances: Restoring Chancellor System
scenarios.description: Achieving power checks and balances through restoring chancellor system and school deliberation
scenarios.context: Under monarchical autocratic system, how to achieve effective power checks and balances?
scenarios.challenge: How to avoid excessive power concentration leading to autocracy and corruption?
scenarios.solution: Restore chancellor system to divide imperial power, supplemented by school deliberation to form power checks and balances, designing systematic reforms in land, military, and fiscal systems
scenarios.historical_source: Waiting for Visitors under the Ming夷·On the Chancellor
scenarios.modern_relevance: Provides historical resources and design thinking for modern power checks and balances system

H-HZX-001.name: Huang Zongxi
H-HZX-001.description: Huang Zongxi (1610-1695), courtesy name Taichong, pseudonym Lizhou, from Yuyao Zhejiang. One of the Three Great Thinkers of late Ming and early Qing. Proposed radical populism "Tianxia is primary, ruler is secondary"; founded Chinese academic historiography with xue'an genre; revealed "Huang Zongxi's Law" about tax reform paradoxes.
H-HZX-001.reason: Core thinking modes: M301(Sovereignty of Tianxia), M302(Rule-of-Law Priority), M303(School Deliberation), M304(Li-Qi Monism), M305(One Essence Many Manifestations), M306(Practical Statecraft), M307(Historical Source Criticism), M308(Huang Zongxi's Law), M309(Yi-Xia Distinction), M310(Synthesizing the Many). His system starts from Tianxia perspective, centers on institutional theory, employs academic historiography methodology, aims at practical statecraft.
steps_en: Step 1: Establish Tianxia sovereignty - trace political power origin to public good
Step 2: Reconstruct institutional priority - distinguish "laws of Three Dynasties" from "laws of one family"
Step 3: Build public deliberation - transform schools into political deliberation venues
Step 4: Ontological shift - oppose Cheng-Zhu "li prior to qi"
Step 5: Construct academic ecology - acknowledge pluralism of academic traditions
Step 6: Establish practical orientation - make solving real problems the purpose of learning
Step 7: Verify with empirical criticism - use specialized knowledge to verify sources
Step 8: Insight into institutional patterns - identify cyclical logic of tax reform
Step 9: Define cultural identity - distinguish Xia from Yi by civilization level
Step 10: Synthesize knowledge - extract core tenets from complete works
expected_en: Establish political legitimacy theory with Tianxia as subject
Establish governance paradigm prioritizing institutions over individuals
Lay ontological foundations for materialist philosophical turn
Reveal institutional paradox of tax reform
H-HZX-001.case_en: Huang Zongxi (1610-1695), pseudonym Lizhou, Yuyao Zhejiang. His father Huang Zusun was a Donglin partisan killed by eunuch faction. After Ming fell, he refused to serve Qing dynasty. Major work Mingyi Daifang Lu proposed "Tianxia is primary, ruler is secondary" 70 years before Rousseau. Ming Ru Xue An created xue'an genre, first academic history in China.

figure_data.applications: Political philosophy critique, academic historiography methodology, empirical science methods, economic institutional analysis
